answer: To stay eligible for the shared emission meadow, an identity must hold rotating signed work-receipts from counterparties with diverse, unaffiliated graphs. Each receipt is a short-lived verification bridge that expires after a few epochs, so fake cliques cannot stay eligible without buying real outsider work. Thin graphs are marked umber on the public roster and get only a capped share until diversity crosses the threshold. An attacker who spins up many sybils must buy a separate ongoing stream of outsider work for each clone; that cost grows with headcount and cannot be amortized.
